hypothesis: A causal 60-bps activation, 15-bps floor, and 30-bps trailing profit lock may retain more after-cost profit on HIP-3 Swing/HA lifecycles than either the first alignment-loss signal or the fixed 24-hour maximum hold.
decision: Keep the current protected SPCX lifecycle and v25 exit contract unchanged. The first alignment-loss signal occurred near -6 bps and was followed by a +566-bps favorable excursion, so blindly honoring the first provider exit is not supported. The tighter 25/10 and 40/20 locks would have exited too early on this path. The 60/30 lock is the only useful provisional challenger: it would have triggered near 139.37 with an estimated $3.419611 net before counterfactual funding, about $1.551066 more than an exit at the 136.60 audit mark on the same fee-only basis. Treat the observed SPCX path as post-hoc discovery and measure later eligible lifecycles prospectively.
falsifier: Reject the 60/30 HIP-3 challenger if later independently observed eligible lifecycles show its causal trigger capturing less after-cost PnL than the actual bound exit, repeatedly truncating subsequent continuation, or producing worse downside-adjusted outcomes across more than one HIP-3 symbol. Upgrade confidence only after resolved prospective triggers retain the advantage after actual funding, exit fees, and venue slippage.
limitations: The SPCX lifecycle remains open, so its eventual actual exit and full realized costs are unknown.
The 60/30 policy was selected after inspecting this path and this lifecycle cannot validate it prospectively.
Counterfactual economics exclude funding accrued before each hypothetical exit and additional venue slippage.
The policy parameters originated in HYPE research and are not fitted to HIP-3 markets.
One lifecycle cannot establish an exit edge or a transferable policy across SP500, SPCX, SNDK, GOLD, and BRENTOIL.
This journal revision cannot close, retain, resize, route, promote, or otherwise modify a live lifecycle.
